data.text: Ephraim feeds on wind and pursues the east wind. All day he multiplies lies and violence. They make a covenant with Assyria, and oil is carried to Egypt.
The LORD has a charge against Judah. He will punish Jacob according to his ways and repay him according to his deeds.
data.titulo: The LORD’s Charge and the Memory of Jacob

data.text: In the womb he grasped his brother by the heel, and in his strength he wrestled with God.
He wrestled with the angel and prevailed; he wept and pleaded with him. He found him at Bethel, and there he spoke with us—
the LORD, the God of hosts; the LORD is his memorial name.
So you, return to your God. Keep steadfast love and justice, and wait continually for your God.
data.titulo: Return to God in Steadfast Love and Justice

data.text: A merchant holds dishonest scales in his hand; he loves to oppress.
Ephraim says, “Surely I have grown rich; I have acquired wealth for myself. In all my labors they will find no guilt in me that is sin.”
“But I am the LORD your God from the land of Egypt. I will again make you dwell in tents, as in the days of the appointed feast.
I spoke to the prophets and multiplied visions. Through the prophets I used comparisons.”
data.titulo: The LORD’s Prophets and Israel’s Response

data.text: If there is iniquity in Gilead, they are surely worthless. In Gilgal they sacrifice bulls; their altars are like heaps of stones in the furrows of the field.
Jacob fled to the country of Aram. Israel served for a wife, and for a wife he tended flocks.
Through a prophet the LORD brought Israel up from Egypt, and through a prophet he was guarded.
Ephraim has bitterly provoked anger. His Lord will leave his bloodguilt upon him and repay him for his reproach.
